pr_title: fix: server.listen listener is not cleanup properly
pr_body:
I don't think we should permit multiple calls to `.listen`, but we should also properly cleanup the listener if `node` currently doesn't.

Fixes #5519 

#### Checklist

- [ ] run `npm run test` and `npm run benchmark`
- [ ] tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [ ] documentation is changed or added
- [ ] commit message and code follows the [Developer's Certification of Origin](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#developers-certificate-of-origin-11)
      and the [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issue_context.title: listen() registers a callback even when listen() fails, calling the callback twice - once when it fails and again if it succeeds in a later call
comments:
This is the line which cause problem.
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/caaeb9fc3a928bb4df4c636468553df135d82edb/lib/server.js#L112

The multiple-calls seems valid to `avvio` API definitions, tho on `fastify` can lead to confusion.
Maybe we can keep some sort of flag per-callback to verify wether or not to call it given the attempt.

We do not mark the server as `failed` when failed to start listening, I imagined was designed with multiple calls in mind?

I think multiple calls make sense in other contexts. Such as when setting up plugins or setting up routes which can hit several functions and the order matters.

But on the listen() function it doesn't seem to make sense to register a callback for when the function can connect. Specially since there is no native mechanism to auto retry the connection, there doesn't seem to be an endpoint to retry the connection with the previous parameters either, and I am unsure if the ready state can change for it to be triggered again.

Also every single point in the documentation points to exiting the process as soon as it fails.

Finally this seems like a problem because after 10 failed attempts to listen() you will get a node warning message stating this:
`(node:22408) MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 listening listeners added to [Server]. MaxListeners is 10. Use emitter.setMaxListeners() to increase limit
(Use 'node --trace-warnings ...' to show where the warning was created)`

Yeah, that's somehow expected given how the `listen` works Today.

I imagine multiple-calls can be helpful in situations when, e.g. you are waiting for a `port` to be freed to listen on it. But there are better ways to manage that.

From my side, I believe it should be fine to avoid multiple-calls to `listen` when an error happened.
We can take advantage of the new major to make it default, and backport a warn in case there are implementations that rely on it Today.

review_comments:
I believe we are safe here without `try-catch`.
The error should go to the error event handler, even if it doesn't `.ready` is a Promise which can catch the error anyway.

`.listening = true` is place inside `listening` event which guarantee to be listening.
